name: fix_python_html_injection_escape
description: HTML injection via unescaped f-string interpolation -> html.escape; incomplete-fix broken hand-replaces < and > only, leaving & and quotes raw
prompts: render_comment(author, body) in render.py interpolates user-supplied author and body straight into an HTML string - a classic stored-XSS hole (<script>...</script> in a comment executes). Fix it by HTML-escaping both values with the standard library's html.escape before interpolation, so <, >, &, and quote characters are all encoded. Do not hand-roll a partial replacement of just < and > - that leaves & and quotes raw, which both mangles legitimate text (Tom & Jerry) and can still break out of an attribute context. The markup structure and class names stay exactly as they are for benign input.

reference_solution.render.py:
import html def render_comment(author, body): """Render a comment as an HTML snippet.""" author = html.escape(author) body = html.escape(body) return ( f"
" f"{author}" f"
